questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force your vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down gently by applying the brakes. Once you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply to force your vehicle back.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, what is important to remember?

options.text: Pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.
Give yourself extra space when stopping.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerously slick, especially right after rain starts. Your vehicle travels on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to keep your wheels from losing traction.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your directional signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal steadily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal steadily.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal steadily. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for nearby police cars.

questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when pavement is wet.
The road ahead has curves and turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the pavement is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or turns, and keep more distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.

questions.question: Another car is about to hit you. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed where the sign is posted.

questions.question: The risk of hydroplaning can be reduced by driving:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving more slowly reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leaving plenty of space between your vehicle and others gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When driving in rain, what should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when it rains.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean? You may stop only when a police officer tells you to, or to:

options.text: Stop for less than five minutes.

questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can stop only to obey a traffic signal, follow a police officer's direction, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: Your vehicle takes longer to stop when stopping on:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on surfaces with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes on the left. Look for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing vehicle can return to the right lane easily.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and vehicles with multiple people.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. Multiple chevron signs may appear along the curve.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop and check for traffic before proceeding. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light ahead is red.
The traffic light ahead is broken.
The traffic light ahead is green.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is at the next intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always give the right of way to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Stay alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: At high speeds, tires cannot clear water from the road effectively. Your vehicle may slide on water instead of gripping the road. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mean you cannot pass other vehicles in that area.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Release the accelerator and slow down gradually. Once you are moving very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: Are placed in every location where there is a present danger.
Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn drivers that they are approaching a school zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do, such as speed limits or turning rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign means left turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the overhead clearance is low.

questions.question: You stop at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: When may you stop your car on railroad tracks?

options.text: If you are crossing and your car cannot completely clear the tracks.
If it sounds like there are no trains nearby.
If the crossing gate is not down.

questions.explanation: Never stop on the tracks. Only cross railroad tracks if your car can completely clear them. If your car stalls on the tracks, get out and push it off if possible. If you cannot move it, get help.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that bicycles may cross here.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to a drink by saying, "No thanks, I'm driving."

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes is to decide before drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is harder to make safe choices after you have been drinking.
